openclaw.configUpdateIntro: Update-channel and startup-check behavior for keeping OpenClaw runtime versions current. Use conservative channels in production and more experimental channels only in controlled environments.
openclaw.configUpdateChannelHelp: Update channel for git + npm installs ("stable", "beta", or "dev").
openclaw.configUpdateCheckOnStartHelp: Check for npm updates when the gateway starts (default: true).
openclaw.configUpdateAutoHeadingDesc: Optional automatic package updates (stable delay, jitter, and beta check interval).
openclaw.configUpdateAutoEnabledHelp: Enable background auto-update for package installs (default: false).
openclaw.configUpdateStableDelayHelp: Minimum delay before stable-channel auto-apply starts (default: 6).
openclaw.configUpdateStableJitterHelp: Extra stable-channel rollout spread window in hours (default: 12).
openclaw.configUpdateBetaIntervalHelp: How often beta-channel checks run in hours (default: 1).
openclaw.configEnvIntro: Environment variables passed to the gateway process.
openclaw.configEnvVarsHelp: Key/value overrides injected into the gateway runtime environment.
openclaw.configShellEnvHelp: Import advanced shell environment values from your login shell during startup.
openclaw.configShellEnvEnabledHelp: Enable shell environment import controls for startup.
openclaw.configShellEnvTimeoutHelp: Maximum wait time for shell env import before fallback.
openclaw.configAuthCooldownsHelp: Cooldown/backoff controls for temporary profile suppression after billing-related failures and retry windows.
openclaw.configAuthBillingBackoffHelp: Base backoff when a profile fails because of billing/insufficient credits (default: 5).
openclaw.configAuthFailureWindowHelp: Failure window used by backoff counters (default: 24).
openclaw.configAuthBackoffOverridesHelp: Optional per-provider billing backoff overrides as JSON object.
openclaw.configMetaLastTouchedAtHelp: Unsupported schema node. Use Raw mode.
openclaw.configMetaLastTouchedVersionHelp: Auto-set when OpenClaw writes the config.
openclaw.configLoggingConsoleLevelHelp: Console-specific log threshold: "silent", "fatal", "error", "warn", "info", "debug", or "trace" for terminal output control.
openclaw.configLoggingFilePathHelp: Optional file path for persisted log output.
openclaw.configLoggingRedactPatternsHelp: Additional custom redact regex patterns as a JSON array.
openclaw.configDiagnosticsIntro: Diagnostics controls for targeted tracing and cache inspection during debugging.
openclaw.configDiagnosticsCacheTraceHelp: Cache-trace logging settings for observing cache decisions and payload context in embedded runs. Enable this temporarily for debugging and disable afterward.
openclaw.configDiagnosticsFilePathHelp: Path where cache trace logs are written.
openclaw.configCliIntro: CLI startup banner controls for title/version line and tagline style behavior.
openclaw.configCliBannerHelp: Keep banner enabled for fast version/context checks, then tune tagline mode to your preferred noise level.
openclaw.configCliTaglineModeHelp: Controls tagline style in CLI startup banner: "random", "default", or "off".
openclaw.configSecretsIntro: Default secret provider aliases, named provider backends, and resolution limits for env, file, and exec-backed secret refs.
openclaw.configSecretsDefaultsHelp: Provider aliases used when a SecretRef omits an explicit provider (per source).
openclaw.configSecretsDefaultEnvHelp: Default provider alias for env-backed refs.
openclaw.configSecretsDefaultExecHelp: Default provider alias for exec-backed refs.
openclaw.configSecretsDefaultFileHelp: Default provider alias for file-backed refs.
openclaw.configSecretsProvidersHelp: Named secret providers (env allowlists, file paths, or exec commands). Each entry must be valid JSON with source "env", "file", or "exec".
openclaw.configSecretsProviderJsonHelp: Provider object, e.g. {"source":"env"} or {"source":"file","path":"/path/to/secrets.json"}. Blur to apply.
openclaw.configSecretsResolutionHelp: Limits applied when resolving secret refs in batches.
openclaw.configSecretsMaxBatchBytesHelp: Maximum total bytes per resolution batch (1–5242880).
openclaw.configSecretsMaxRefsPerProviderHelp: Maximum refs resolved per provider in one batch (1–4096).
openclaw.configSettingsBlurbBody: Pick a category tab above to edit. The full config file is not shown here — use Raw to view or edit JSON.
openclaw.configSectionNoFormTitle: No form for this section yet
openclaw.configSectionNoFormHint: Switch to Raw to edit the full configuration as JSON.
openclaw.configAcpIntro: ACP runtime controls for agent allowlisting used by ACP sessions.
openclaw.configAcpAllowedAgentsHelp: Allowlist of ACP target agent ids permitted for ACP runtime sessions. Empty means no additional allowlist restriction.
openclaw.configAcpNoItems: No items yet. Click "Add" to create one.
openclaw.configBroadcastIntro: Broadcast routing map for sending the same outbound message to multiple peer IDs per source conversation. Keep this minimal and audited because one source can fan out to many destinations.
openclaw.configBroadcastStrategyHelp: Delivery order for broadcast fan-out: "parallel" sends to all targets concurrently, while "sequential" sends one-by-one. Use "parallel" for speed and "sequential" for stricter ordering/backpressure control.
openclaw.configBroadcastDestinationsHelp: Per-source broadcast destination list: each key is a source peer ID and the value is an array of destination peer IDs. Edit as JSON (excluding strategy). Blur the field to apply.
openclaw.configChannelsEntryJsonHelp: JSON value for this extension channel. Blur to apply.
openclaw.configMessagesAckEmojiHelp: Emoji reaction used to acknowledge inbound messages (empty disables).
openclaw.configMessagesAckScopeHelp: When to send ack reactions ("group-mentions", "group-all", "direct", "all", "off", "none"). "off"/"none" disables ack reactions entirely.
openclaw.configMessagesRemoveAckHelp: Removes the acknowledgment reaction after final reply delivery when enabled.
openclaw.configTalkApiKeyHelp: Use this legacy ElevenLabs API key for Talk mode only during migration, and keep secrets in env-backed storage. Prefer talk.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey (fallback: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY).
openclaw.configTalkElevenlabsApiKeyHelp: Provider API key for Talk mode. Prefer env-backed secret refs when possible.
openclaw.configTalkVoiceIdHelp: Legacy ElevenLabs default voice ID for Talk mode. Prefer talk.providers.elevenlabs.voiceId.
openclaw.configTalkModelIdHelp: Legacy ElevenLabs model ID for Talk mode (default: eleven_v3). Prefer talk.providers.elevenlabs.modelId.
openclaw.configTalkOutputFormatHelp: Use this legacy ElevenLabs output format for Talk mode (for example pcm_44100 or mp3_44100_128) only during migration. Prefer talk.providers.elevenlabs.outputFormat.
openclaw.configTalkVoiceAliasesHelp: Legacy ElevenLabs voice alias map as JSON (string → string). Prefer talk.providers.elevenlabs.voiceAliases. Blur to apply.
openclaw.configTalkInterruptHelp: If true (default), stop assistant speech when the user starts speaking in Talk mode.
openclaw.configTalkSilenceTimeoutHelp: Milliseconds of user silence before Talk mode finalizes and sends the current transcript. Leave empty for platform default.
openclaw.configAudioTranscriptionIntro: Command-based transcription settings for converting audio files into text before agent handling. Keep a simple, deterministic command path here so failures are easy to diagnose in logs.
openclaw.configAudioTranscriptionCommandHelp: Executable + args used to transcribe audio (first token must be a safe binary/path), for example ["whisper-cli", "--model", "small", "{input}"]. Prefer a pinned command so runtime environments behave consistently.
openclaw.configAudioCommandArgsHint: One input field per argv token (executable first).
openclaw.configAudioTranscriptionTimeoutHelp: Maximum time allowed for the transcription command to finish before it is aborted. Increase this for longer recordings, and keep it tight in latency-sensitive deployments.
openclaw.configSatelliteIntro: These section tabs mirror the OpenClaw Control UI for this settings page. Each tab corresponds to a top-level configuration area in openclaw.json.
openclaw.configSatelliteRootIntro: Overview for this settings area. Select a section tab to focus a category, or use Raw to edit the full configuration.
openclaw.configSatelliteRootHint: Choose a section tab (for example Channels or Messages on Communication) to jump to that part of the config, or open Raw for JSON.
openclaw.configSatelliteFormHint: Schema-driven forms for this category are not implemented in this plugin yet. Switch to Raw to edit the full configuration as JSON.
openclaw.configAppearanceModeHint: Choose light or dark mode for the selected theme.
openclaw.configUiAccentColorHelp: Primary accent/seam color used by UI surfaces for emphasis, badges, and visual identity cues. Use high-contrast values that remain readable across light/dark themes.
openclaw.configUiAssistantGroupHelp: Assistant display identity settings for name and avatar shown in UI surfaces. Keep these values aligned with your operator-facing persona and support expectations.
openclaw.configUiAssistantNameHelp: Display name shown for the assistant in UI views, chat chrome, and status contexts. Keep this stable so operators can reliably identify which assistant persona is active.
openclaw.configUiAssistantAvatarHelp: Assistant avatar image source used in UI surfaces (URL, path, or data URI depending on runtime support). Use trusted assets and consistent branding dimensions for clean rendering.
openclaw.configWizardSectionHelp: Setup wizard state tracking fields that record the most recent guided onboarding run details. Keep these fields for observability and troubleshooting of setup flows across upgrades.
openclaw.configWizardLastRunAtHelp: ISO timestamp for when the setup wizard most recently completed on this host. Use this to confirm onboarding recency during support and operational audits.
openclaw.configWizardLastRunVersionHelp: OpenClaw version recorded at the time of the most recent wizard run on this config. Use this when diagnosing behavior differences across version-to-version onboarding changes.
openclaw.configWizardLastRunCommitHelp: Source commit identifier recorded for the last wizard execution in development builds. Use this to correlate onboarding behavior with exact source state during debugging.
openclaw.configWizardLastRunCommandHelp: Command invocation recorded for the latest wizard run to preserve execution context. Use this to reproduce onboarding steps when verifying setup regressions.
openclaw.configWizardLastRunModeHelp: Wizard execution mode recorded as "local" or "remote" for the most recent onboarding flow. Use this to understand whether setup targeted direct local runtime or remote gateway topology.
openclaw.configCommandsSectionHelp: Controls chat command surfaces, owner gating, and elevated command access behavior across providers. Keep defaults unless you need stricter operator controls or broader command availability.
openclaw.configCommandsNativeHelp: Registers native slash/menu commands with channels that support command registration (Discord, Slack, Telegram). Keep enabled for discoverability unless you intentionally run text-only command workflows.
openclaw.configCommandsNativeSkillsHelp: Registers native skill commands so users can invoke skills directly from provider command menus where supported. Keep aligned with your skill policy so exposed commands match what operators expect.
openclaw.configCommandsTextHelp: Enables text-command parsing in chat input in addition to native command surfaces where available. Keep this enabled for compatibility across channels that do not support native command registration.
openclaw.configCommandsBashHelp: Allow bash chat command (`!`; `/bash` alias) to run host shell commands (default: false; requires tools.elevated).
openclaw.configCommandsBashForegroundHelp: How long bash waits before backgrounding (default: 2000; 0 backgrounds immediately).
openclaw.configCommandsConfigHelp: Allow /config chat command to read/write config on disk (default: false).
openclaw.configCommandsDebugHelp: Allow /debug chat command for runtime-only overrides (default: false).
openclaw.configCommandsRestartHelp: Allow /restart and gateway restart tool actions (default: true).
openclaw.configCommandsOwnerAllowFromHelp: Explicit owner allowlist for owner-only tools/commands. Use channel-native IDs (optionally prefixed like "whatsapp:+15551234567"). '*' is ignored.
openclaw.configCommandsOwnerDisplayHelp: Controls how owner IDs are rendered in the system prompt. Allowed values: raw, hash. Default: raw.
openclaw.configCommandsOwnerDisplaySecretHelp: Optional secret used to HMAC hash owner IDs when ownerDisplay=hash. Prefer env substitution.
openclaw.configCommandsAllowFromHelp: Defines elevated command allow rules by channel and sender for owner-level command surfaces. Use narrow provider-specific identities so privileged commands are not exposed to broad chat audiences.
openclaw.configApprovalsIntro: Approval routing controls for forwarding exec approval requests to chat destinations outside the originating session. Keep this disabled unless operators need explicit out-of-band approval visibility.
openclaw.configApprovalsExecGroupIntro: Groups exec-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Configure here when approval prompts must reach operational channels instead of only the origin thread.
openclaw.configApprovalsExecEnabledHelp: Enables forwarding of exec approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Keep disabled in low-risk setups and enable only when human approval responders need channel-visible prompts.
openclaw.configApprovalsExecModeHelp: Controls where approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths. Use "session" as baseline and expand only when operational workflow requires redundancy.
openclaw.configApprovalsAgentFilterHelp: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to limit forwarding blast radius and avoid notifying channels for unrelated agents.
openclaw.configApprovalsSessionFilterHelp: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded to shared destinations.
openclaw.configApprovalsTargetsHelp: Explicit delivery targets used when forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details. Keep target lists least-privilege and validate each destination before enabling broad forwarding.
openclaw.configApprovalsTargetsEmpty: No forwarding targets yet. Use Add to append a JSON target row.
openclaw.configHooksIntro: Inbound webhook automation surface for mapping external events into wake or agent actions in OpenClaw. Keep this locked down with explicit token/session/agent controls before exposing it beyond trusted networks.
openclaw.configHooksAllowedAgentIdsHelp: Allowlist of agent IDs that hook mappings are allowed to target when selecting execution agents. Use this to constrain automation events to dedicated service agents.
openclaw.configHooksAllowedAgentIdsEmpty: No entries yet. Use Add to include an agent id.
openclaw.configHooksEnabledHelp: Enables the hooks endpoint and mapping execution pipeline for inbound webhook requests. Keep disabled unless you are actively routing external events into the gateway.
openclaw.configHooksPathHelp: HTTP path used by the hooks endpoint (for example `/hooks`) on the gateway control server. Use a non-guessable path and combine it with token validation for defense in depth.
openclaw.configHooksTokenHelp: Shared bearer token checked by hooks ingress for request authentication before mappings run. Use environment substitution and rotate regularly when webhook endpoints are internet-accessible.
openclaw.configHooksDefaultSessionKeyHelp: Fallback session key used for hook deliveries when a request does not provide one through allowed channels. Use a stable but scoped key to avoid mixing unrelated automation conversations.
openclaw.configHooksAllowRequestSessionKeyHelp: Allows callers to supply a session key in hook requests when true, enabling caller-controlled routing. Keep false unless trusted integrators explicitly need custom session threading.
openclaw.configHooksMaxBodyBytesHelp: Maximum accepted webhook payload size in bytes before the request is rejected. Keep this bounded to reduce abuse risk and protect memory usage under bursty integrations.
openclaw.configHooksTransformsDirHelp: Base directory for hook transform modules referenced by mapping transform.module paths. Use a controlled repo directory so dynamic imports remain reviewable and predictable.
openclaw.configHooksAllowedSessionKeyPrefixesHelp: Allowlist of accepted session-key prefixes for inbound hook requests when caller-provided keys are enabled. Use narrow prefixes to prevent arbitrary session-key injection.
openclaw.configHooksPresetsHelp: Named hook preset bundles applied at load time to seed standard mappings and behavior defaults. Keep preset usage explicit so operators can audit which automations are active.
openclaw.configHooksMappingsHelp: Ordered mapping rules that match inbound hook requests and choose wake or agent actions with optional delivery routing. Use specific mappings first to avoid broad pattern rules capturing everything.
openclaw.configHooksGmailHelp: Gmail push integration settings (Pub/Sub, optional local serve). Edit as JSON; leave {} to omit.
openclaw.configHooksInternalHelp: Internal hook handlers, entries, load paths, and installs. Edit as JSON; leave {} to omit.
openclaw.configBindingsIntro: Top-level binding rules for routing and persistent ACP conversation ownership. Use type=route for normal routing and type=acp for persistent ACP harness bindings.
openclaw.configBindingsAdvancedHelp: Each entry is one binding object (route or ACP). Use JSON per row; omit type or set "route" for normal routing, or "type": "acp" with match.peer for ACP bindings.
openclaw.configBindingsEmpty: No binding entries yet. Use Add to append a route template.
openclaw.configCronIntro: Global scheduler settings for stored cron jobs, run concurrency, delivery fallback, and run-session retention. Keep defaults unless you are scaling job volume or integrating external webhook receivers.
openclaw.configCronEnabledHelp: Enables cron job execution for stored schedules managed by the gateway. Keep enabled for normal reminder/automation flows, and disable only to pause all cron execution without deleting jobs.
openclaw.configCronStoreHelp: Path to the cron job store file used to persist scheduled jobs across restarts. Set an explicit path only when you need custom storage layout, backups, or mounted volumes.
openclaw.configCronMaxConcurrentRunsHelp: Limits how many cron jobs can execute at the same time when multiple schedules fire together. Use lower values to protect CPU/memory under heavy automation load, or raise carefully for higher throughput.
openclaw.configCronSessionRetentionHelp: Controls how long completed cron run sessions are kept before pruning (`24h`, `7d`, `1h30m`, or `false` to disable pruning; default: `24h`). Use shorter retention to reduce storage growth on high-frequency schedules.
openclaw.configCronRetryHelp: Overrides the default retry policy for one-shot jobs when they fail with transient errors (rate limit, overloaded, network, server_error). Omit to use defaults: maxAttempts 3, backoffMs [30000, 60000, 300000], retry all transient types.
openclaw.configCronRetryMaxAttemptsHelp: Max retries for one-shot jobs on transient errors before permanent disable (default: 3).
openclaw.configCronRetryBackoffMsHelp: Backoff delays in ms for each retry attempt (default: [30000, 60000, 300000]). Use shorter values for faster retries.
openclaw.configCronRetryRetryOnHelp: Error types to retry: rate_limit, overloaded, network, timeout, server_error. Use to restrict which errors trigger retries; omit to retry all transient types.
openclaw.configCronWebhookHelp: Deprecated legacy fallback webhook URL used only for old jobs with `notify=true`. Migrate to per-job delivery using `delivery.mode="webhook"` plus `delivery.to`, and avoid relying on this global field.
openclaw.configCronWebhookTokenHelp: Bearer token attached to cron webhook POST deliveries when webhook mode is used. Prefer secret/env substitution and rotate this token regularly if shared webhook endpoints are internet-reachable.
openclaw.configCronRunLogHelp: Pruning controls for per-job cron run history files under `cron/runs/<jobId>.jsonl`, including size and line retention.
openclaw.configCronRunLogMaxBytesHelp: Maximum bytes per cron run-log file before pruning rewrites to the last keepLines entries (for example `2mb`, default `2000000`).
openclaw.configCronRunLogKeepLinesHelp: How many trailing run-log lines to retain when a file exceeds maxBytes (default `2000`). Increase for longer forensic history or lower for smaller disks.
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertGroupHelp: Optional alerts after repeated job failures (gateway-managed).
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertEnabledHelp: When enabled, emit alerts according to after/cooldown/mode after consecutive failures.
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertAfterHelp: Minimum consecutive failures before alerting (must be at least 1).
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertCooldownHelp: Minimum time between alerts for the same condition.
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertModeHelp: announce or webhook delivery for failure alerts.
openclaw.configCronFailureAlertAccountIdHelp: Optional account selector for multi-account channel delivery.
openclaw.configCronFailureDestinationGroupHelp: Optional routing for failure notifications (channel, destination, mode).
openclaw.configCronFailureDestAccountIdHelp: Optional account id when the channel has multiple accounts.
openclaw.configCronFailureDestModeHelp: announce or webhook for failure destination delivery.
openclaw.configPluginsEnabledHelp: Enable or disable plugin/extension loading globally during startup and config reload (default: true). Keep enabled only when extension capabilities are required by your deployment.
openclaw.configPluginsAllowHelp: Optional allowlist of plugin IDs; when set, only listed plugins are eligible to load. Use this to enforce approved extension inventories in controlled environments.
openclaw.configPluginsDenyHelp: Optional denylist of plugin IDs that are blocked even if allowlists or paths include them. Use deny rules for emergency rollback and hard blocks on risky plugins.
openclaw.configPluginsAllowEmpty: No allowlist entries yet. Use Add to include a plugin id.
openclaw.configPluginsDenyEmpty: No denylist entries yet. Use Add to include a plugin id.
openclaw.configGatewayIntro: Gateway runtime surface for bind mode, auth, control UI, remote transport, and operational safety controls. Keep conservative defaults unless you intentionally expose the gateway beyond trusted local interfaces.
openclaw.configGatewayPortHelp: TCP port used by the gateway listener for API, control UI, and channel-facing ingress paths. Use a dedicated port and avoid collisions with reverse proxies or local developer services.
openclaw.configGatewayModeHelp: Gateway operation mode: "local" runs channels and agent runtime on this host, while "remote" connects through remote transport. Keep "local" unless you intentionally run a split remote gateway topology.
openclaw.configGatewayBindHelp: Network bind profile: "auto", "lan", "loopback", "custom", or "tailnet" to control interface exposure. Keep "loopback" or "auto" for safest local operation unless external clients must connect.
openclaw.configGatewayCustomBindHostHelp: Explicit bind host/IP used when gateway.bind is set to custom for manual interface targeting. Use a precise address and avoid wildcard binds unless external exposure is required.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiEnabledHelp: Enables serving the gateway Control UI from the gateway HTTP process when true. Keep enabled for local administration, and disable when an external control surface replaces it.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiBasePathHelp: HTTP path prefix where the Control UI is served.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiRootHelp: Filesystem root for Control UI static assets when customized.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiAllowedOriginsHelp: Browser origin allowlist for Control UI / WebChat websocket checks. JSON array of strings.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiDangerHostHelp: DANGEROUS toggle that enables Host-header based origin fallback for Control UI/WebChat websocket checks.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiInsecureAuthHelp: Relaxes auth checks for non-TLS deployments. Use only in trusted local setups.
openclaw.configGatewayControlUiDisableDeviceAuthH: DANGEROUS: disables device pairing auth for Control UI paths.
openclaw.configGatewayAuthModeHelp: Gateway auth mode: "none", "token", "password", or "trusted-proxy" depending on your edge architecture.
openclaw.configGatewayAuthTokenHelp: Shared token for gateway HTTP/WebSocket auth when auth.mode is token.
openclaw.configGatewayAuthPasswordHelp: Password for gateway auth when auth.mode is password.
openclaw.configGatewayAuthAllowTailscaleHelp: Allows trusted Tailscale identity paths to satisfy gateway auth checks when configured.
openclaw.configGatewayAuthRateLimitHelp: Login/auth attempt throttling (JSON object: maxAttempts, windowMs, lockoutMs, exemptLoopback).
openclaw.configGatewayAuthTrustedProxyHelp: Trusted-proxy auth header mapping (JSON: userHeader, requiredHeaders?, allowUsers?).
openclaw.configGatewayTrustedProxiesHelp: CIDR/IP allowlist of upstream proxies permitted to provide forwarded client identity headers. JSON array of strings.
openclaw.configGatewayAllowRealIpFallbackHelp: Enables x-real-ip fallback when x-forwarded-for is missing in proxy scenarios. Keep disabled unless your ingress stack requires this compatibility behavior.
openclaw.configGatewayToolsAllowHelp: Explicit gateway-level tool allowlist when you want a narrow set of tools available at runtime.
openclaw.configGatewayToolsDenyHelp: Explicit gateway-level tool denylist to block risky tools even if lower-level policies allow them.
openclaw.configGatewayToolsAllowEmpty: No allowlist tool entries. Use Add.
openclaw.configGatewayToolsDenyEmpty: No denylist tool entries. Use Add.
openclaw.configGatewayChannelHealthHelp: Interval in minutes for automatic channel health probing and status updates.
openclaw.configGatewayTailscaleResetHelp: Resets Tailscale Serve/Funnel state on gateway exit to avoid stale published routes after shutdown.
openclaw.configGatewayRemoteUrlHelp: Remote Gateway WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://).
openclaw.configGatewayRemoteTokenHelp: Bearer token for remote gateway token auth.
openclaw.configGatewayRemotePasswordHelp: Password for remote gateway when password auth is used.
openclaw.configGatewayRemoteTlsFpHelp: Expected sha256 TLS fingerprint for the remote gateway (pin to avoid MITM).
openclaw.configGatewayRemoteSshIdentityHelp: Optional SSH identity file path (passed to ssh -i).
openclaw.configGatewayReloadModeHelp: Live config-reload policy: off, restart, hot, or hybrid.
openclaw.configGatewayReloadDebounceHelp: Debounce delay in milliseconds before applying config reload.
openclaw.configGatewayTlsEnabledHelp: Enables TLS termination at the gateway listener so clients connect over HTTPS/WSS directly.
openclaw.configGatewayTlsAutoGenHelp: Auto-generates a local TLS certificate/key pair when explicit files are not configured.
openclaw.configGatewayTlsCertPathHelp: Filesystem path to the TLS certificate file.
openclaw.configGatewayTlsKeyPathHelp: Filesystem path to the TLS private key file.
openclaw.configGatewayTlsCaPathHelp: Optional CA bundle path for custom trust-chain requirements.
openclaw.configWebIntro: Web channel runtime settings for heartbeat and reconnect behavior when operating web-based chat surfaces. Use reconnect values tuned to your network reliability profile and expected uptime needs.
openclaw.configWebEnabledHelp: Enables the web channel runtime and related websocket lifecycle behavior. Keep disabled when web chat is unused to reduce active connection management overhead.
openclaw.configWebHeartbeatHelp: Heartbeat interval in seconds for web channel connectivity and liveness maintenance. Use shorter intervals for faster detection, or longer intervals to reduce keepalive chatter.
openclaw.configWebReconnectHelp: Reconnect backoff policy for web channel reconnect attempts after transport failure. Keep bounded retries and jitter tuned to avoid thundering-herd reconnect behavior.
openclaw.configWebReconnectInitialMsHelp: Initial reconnect delay in milliseconds before the first retry after disconnection. Use modest delays to recover quickly without immediate retry storms.
openclaw.configWebReconnectMaxMsHelp: Maximum reconnect backoff cap in milliseconds to bound retry delay growth over repeated failures. Use a reasonable cap so recovery remains timely after prolonged outages.
openclaw.configWebReconnectFactorHelp: Exponential backoff multiplier used between reconnect attempts in web channel retry loops. Keep factor above 1 and tune with jitter for stable large-fleet reconnect behavior.
openclaw.configWebReconnectJitterHelp: Randomization factor (0-1) applied to reconnect delays to desynchronize clients after outage events. Keep non-zero jitter in multi-client deployments to reduce synchronized spikes.
openclaw.configWebReconnectMaxAttemptsHelp: Maximum reconnect attempts before giving up for the current failure sequence (0 means no retries). Use finite caps for controlled failure handling in automation-sensitive environments.
openclaw.configBrowserIntro: Browser runtime controls for local or remote CDP attachment, profile routing, and screenshot/snapshot behavior. Keep defaults unless your automation workflow requires custom browser transport settings.
openclaw.configBrowserEnabledHelp: Enables browser capability wiring in the gateway so browser tools and CDP-driven workflows can run. Disable when browser automation is not needed to reduce surface area and startup work.
openclaw.configBrowserEvaluateEnabledHelp: Enables browser-side evaluate helpers for runtime script evaluation capabilities where supported. Keep disabled unless your workflows require evaluate semantics beyond snapshots/navigation.
openclaw.configBrowserAttachOnlyHelp: Restricts browser mode to attach-only behavior without starting local browser processes. Use this when all browser sessions are externally managed by a remote CDP provider.
openclaw.configBrowserHeadlessHelp: Forces browser launch in headless mode when the local launcher starts browser instances. Keep headless enabled for server environments and disable only when visible UI debugging is required.
openclaw.configBrowserNoSandboxHelp: Disables Chromium sandbox isolation flags for environments where sandboxing fails at runtime. Keep this off whenever possible because process isolation protections are reduced.
openclaw.configBrowserCdpUrlHelp: Remote CDP websocket URL used to attach to an externally managed browser instance. Use this for centralized browser hosts and keep URL access restricted to trusted network paths.
openclaw.configBrowserRemoteCdpTimeoutMsHelp: Timeout in milliseconds for connecting to a remote CDP endpoint before failing the browser attach attempt. Increase for high-latency tunnels, or lower for faster failure detection.
openclaw.configBrowserRemoteCdpHandshakeTimeoutMs: Timeout in milliseconds for post-connect CDP handshake readiness checks against remote browser targets. Raise this for slow-start remote browsers and lower to fail fast in automation loops.
openclaw.configBrowserCdpPortRangeStartHelp: Starting local CDP port used for auto-allocated browser profile ports. Increase this when host-level port defaults conflict with other local services.
openclaw.configBrowserDefaultProfileHelp: Default browser profile name selected when callers do not explicitly choose a profile. Use a stable low-privilege profile as the default to reduce accidental cross-context state use.
openclaw.configBrowserExecutablePathHelp: Explicit browser executable path when auto-discovery is insufficient for your host environment. Use absolute stable paths so launch behavior stays deterministic across restarts.
openclaw.configBrowserColorHelp: Default accent color used for browser profile/UI cues where colored identity hints are displayed. Use consistent colors to help operators identify active browser profile context quickly.
openclaw.configBrowserRelayBindHostHelp: Bind IP address for the Chrome extension relay listener. Leave unset for loopback-only access, or set an explicit non-loopback IP such as 0.0.0.0 only when the relay must be reachable across network namespaces (for example WSL2) and the surrounding network is already trusted.
openclaw.configBrowserExtraArgsHelp: JSON array of extra Chromium launch arguments (strings). Example: ["--disable-gpu"]. Leave empty to omit.
openclaw.configBrowserProfilesHelp: Named browser profile connection map (JSON object) for routing to CDP ports or URLs with optional metadata. Profile keys must match ^[a-z0-9-]+$.
openclaw.configBrowserSnapshotDefaultsHelp: Default snapshot capture configuration used when callers do not provide explicit snapshot options. Tune this for consistent capture behavior across channels and automation paths.
openclaw.configBrowserSnapshotModeHelp: Default snapshot extraction mode controlling how page content is transformed for agent consumption. Choose the mode that balances readability, fidelity, and token footprint for your workflows.
openclaw.configBrowserSsrfPolicyHelp: Server-side request forgery guardrail settings for browser/network fetch paths that could reach internal hosts. Keep restrictive defaults in production and open only explicitly approved targets.
openclaw.configBrowserSsrfAllowPrivateNetworkHelp: Legacy alias for browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork. Prefer the dangerously-named key so risk intent is explicit.
openclaw.configBrowserSsrfDangerouslyAllowPrivate: Allows access to private-network address ranges from browser tooling. Default is enabled for trusted-network operator setups; disable to enforce strict public-only resolution checks.
openclaw.configBrowserSsrfAllowedHostnamesHelp: Explicit hostname allowlist exceptions for SSRF policy checks on browser/network requests. Keep this list minimal and review entries regularly to avoid stale broad access.
openclaw.configBrowserSsrfHostnameAllowlistHelp: Legacy/alternate hostname allowlist field used by SSRF policy consumers for explicit host exceptions. Use stable exact hostnames and avoid wildcard-like broad patterns.
openclaw.configNodeHostSectionMeta: Node host and browser proxy routing
openclaw.configNodeHostIntro: Node host controls for features exposed from this gateway node to other nodes or clients. Keep defaults unless you intentionally proxy local capabilities across your node network.
openclaw.configNodeHostBrowserProxyHelp: Groups browser-proxy settings for exposing local browser control through node routing. Enable only when remote node workflows need your local browser profiles.
openclaw.configNodeHostBrowserProxyEnabledHelp: Expose the local browser control server through node proxy routing so remote clients can use this host's browser capabilities. Keep disabled unless remote automation explicitly depends on it.
openclaw.configNodeHostBrowserProxyAllowProfilesH: Optional allowlist of browser profile names exposed through node proxy routing. Leave empty to expose all configured profiles, or use a tight list to enforce least-privilege profile access.
openclaw.configCanvasHostIntro: Canvas host settings for serving canvas assets and local live-reload behavior used by canvas-enabled workflows. Keep disabled unless canvas-hosted assets are actively used.
openclaw.configCanvasHostEnabledHelp: Enables the canvas host server process and routes for serving canvas files. Keep disabled when canvas workflows are inactive to reduce exposed local services.
openclaw.configCanvasHostRootHelp: Filesystem root directory served by canvas host for canvas content and static assets. Use a dedicated directory and avoid broad repo roots for least-privilege file exposure.
openclaw.configCanvasHostPortHelp: TCP port used by the canvas host HTTP server when canvas hosting is enabled. Choose a non-conflicting port and align firewall/proxy policy accordingly.
openclaw.configCanvasHostLiveReloadHelp: Enables automatic live-reload behavior for canvas assets during development workflows. Keep disabled in production-like environments where deterministic output is preferred.
openclaw.configDiscoveryIntro: Service discovery settings for local mDNS advertisement and optional wide-area presence signaling. Keep discovery scoped to expected networks to avoid leaking service metadata.
openclaw.configDiscoveryMdnsGroupHelp: mDNS discovery configuration group for local network advertisement and discovery behavior tuning. Keep minimal mode for routine LAN discovery unless extra metadata is required.
openclaw.configDiscoveryMdnsModeHelp: mDNS broadcast mode ("minimal" default, "full" includes cliPath/sshPort, "off" disables mDNS).
openclaw.configDiscoveryWideAreaGroupHelp: Wide-area discovery configuration group for exposing discovery signals beyond local-link scopes. Enable only in deployments that intentionally aggregate gateway presence across sites.
openclaw.configDiscoveryWideAreaEnabledHelp: Enables wide-area discovery signaling when your environment needs non-local gateway discovery. Keep disabled unless cross-network discovery is operationally required.
openclaw.configDiscoveryWideAreaDomainHelp: Optional unicast DNS-SD domain for wide-area discovery, such as openclaw.internal. Use this when you intentionally publish gateway discovery beyond local mDNS scopes.
openclaw.configMediaIntro: Top-level media behavior shared across providers and tools that handle inbound files. Keep defaults unless you need stable filenames for external processing pipelines or longer-lived inbound media retention.
openclaw.configMediaPreserveFilenamesHelp: When enabled, uploaded media keeps its original filename instead of a generated temp-safe name. Turn this on when downstream automations depend on stable names, and leave off to reduce accidental filename leakage.
openclaw.configMediaTtlHoursHelp: Optional retention window in hours for persisted inbound media cleanup across the full media tree. Leave unset to preserve legacy behavior, or set values like 24 (1 day) or 168 (7 days) when you want automatic cleanup.
openclaw.configAgentsIntro: Agent runtime configuration root covering defaults and explicit agent entries used for routing and execution context. Keep this section explicit so model/tool behavior stays predictable across multi-agent workflows.
openclaw.configAgentsDefaultsGroupHelp: Shared default settings inherited by agents unless overridden per entry in agents.list. Use defaults to enforce consistent baseline behavior and reduce duplicated per-agent configuration.
openclaw.configAgentsDefaultsJsonHelp: Edit agents.defaults as a JSON object. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configAgentsListGroupHelp: Explicit list of configured agents with IDs and optional overrides for model, tools, identity, and workspace. Keep IDs stable over time so bindings, approvals, and session routing remain deterministic.
openclaw.configAgentsListJsonHelp: Edit agents.list as a JSON array of agent entries. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configModelsIntro: Model catalog root for provider definitions, merge/replace behavior, and optional Bedrock discovery integration. Keep provider definitions explicit and validated before relying on production failover paths.
openclaw.configModelsModeHelp: Controls provider catalog behavior: "merge" keeps built-ins and overlays your custom providers, while "replace" uses only your configured providers. In "merge", matching provider IDs preserve non-empty agent models.json baseUrl values, while apiKey values are preserved only when the provider is not SecretRef-managed in current config/auth-profile context; SecretRef-managed providers refresh apiKey from current source markers, and matching model contextWindow/maxTokens use the higher value between explicit and implicit entries.
openclaw.configModelsProvidersGroupHelp: Provider map keyed by provider ID containing connection/auth settings and concrete model definitions. Use stable provider keys so references from agents and tooling remain portable across environments.
openclaw.configModelsProvidersJsonHelp: Edit models.providers as a JSON object keyed by provider ID. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockGroupHelp: Automatic AWS Bedrock model discovery settings used to synthesize provider model entries from account visibility. Keep discovery scoped and refresh intervals conservative to reduce API churn.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockEnabledHelp: Enables periodic Bedrock model discovery and catalog refresh for Bedrock-backed providers. Keep disabled unless Bedrock is actively used and IAM permissions are correctly configured.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockRegionHelp: AWS region used for Bedrock discovery calls when discovery is enabled for your deployment. Use the region where your Bedrock models are provisioned to avoid empty discovery results.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockProviderFilterHelp: Optional provider allowlist as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["bedrock"]). Empty or "[]" clears the filter. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockRefreshHelp: Refresh cadence for Bedrock discovery polling in seconds to detect newly available models over time. Use longer intervals in production to reduce API cost and control-plane noise.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockCtxHelp: Fallback context-window value applied to discovered models when provider metadata lacks explicit limits. Use realistic defaults to avoid oversized prompts that exceed true provider constraints.
openclaw.configModelsBedrockMaxTokensHelp: Fallback max-token value applied to discovered models without explicit output token limits. Use conservative defaults to reduce truncation surprises and unexpected token spend.
openclaw.configSkillsIntro: Configure bundled skill allowlists, per-skill overrides, extra load paths, install preferences, and optional limits. Keep allowlists explicit in production so only intended skills ship in prompts and on disk.
openclaw.configSkillsAllowBundledEmpty: No items yet. Click "Add" to create one.
openclaw.configSkillsEntryJsonHelp: Skill entry: optional enabled, apiKey, env map, and config map. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configSkillsExtraDirsEmpty: No extra directories. Click "Add" to add a path.
openclaw.configSkillsLoadWatchHelp: Enable filesystem watching for skill-definition changes so updates can be applied without full process restart. Keep enabled in development workflows and disable in immutable production images.
openclaw.configSkillsLoadDebounceHelp: Debounce window in milliseconds for coalescing rapid skill file changes before reload logic runs. Increase to reduce reload churn on frequent writes, or lower for faster edit feedback.
openclaw.configSkillsInstallPreferBrewHelp: When installing skill tooling, prefer Homebrew where applicable for your environment.
openclaw.configSkillsInstallNodeManagerHelp: Package manager used when skill installs require Node (npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun).
openclaw.configSkillsLimitsIntro: Optional caps for candidate discovery, loaded skills per source, prompt size, and skill file reads.
openclaw.configSkillsLimitMaxCandidatesHelp: Maximum skill candidates considered per discovery root (minimum 1 when set).
openclaw.configSkillsLimitMaxLoadedHelp: Upper bound on skills loaded from a single source (minimum 1 when set).
openclaw.configSkillsLimitMaxInPromptHelp: Maximum number of skills injected into the prompt (0 or more when set).
openclaw.configSkillsLimitMaxPromptCharsHelp: Maximum characters of skill prompt material (0 or more when set).
openclaw.configSkillsLimitMaxFileBytesHelp: Maximum size in bytes for a single skill file read (0 or more when set).
openclaw.configToolsIntro: Global tool access policy and capability configuration across web, exec, media, messaging, and elevated surfaces. Use this section to constrain risky capabilities before broad rollout.
openclaw.configToolsAgentToAgentHelp: Policy for allowing agent-to-agent tool calls and constraining which target agents can be reached. Keep disabled or tightly scoped unless cross-agent orchestration is intentionally enabled.
openclaw.configToolsAgentToAgentEnabledHelp: Enables the agent_to_agent tool surface so one agent can invoke another agent at runtime. Keep off in simple deployments and enable only when orchestration value outweighs complexity.
openclaw.configToolsAgentToAgentAllowEmpty: No items yet. Click "Add" to create one.
openclaw.configToolsProfileHelp: Global tool profile name used to select a predefined tool policy baseline before applying allow/deny overrides. Use this for consistent environment posture across agents and keep profile names stable.
openclaw.configToolsAllowHelp: Absolute tool allowlist that replaces profile-derived defaults for strict environments. Use this only when you intentionally run a tightly curated subset of tool capabilities. Do not combine with "Also allow" in the same scope.
openclaw.configToolsAlsoAllowHelp: Extra tool allowlist entries merged on top of the selected tool profile and default policy. Keep this list small and explicit so audits can quickly identify intentional policy exceptions. Do not combine with "Allow" in the same scope.
openclaw.configToolsDenyHelp: Global tool denylist that blocks listed tools even when profile or provider rules would allow them. Use deny rules for emergency lockouts and long-term defense-in-depth.
openclaw.configToolsListEmpty: No items yet. Click "Add" to create one.
openclaw.configToolsSessionsVisibilityHelp: Controls which sessions can be targeted by sessions_list/sessions_history/sessions_send. Cross-agent still requires tools.agentToAgent when applicable.
openclaw.configToolsByProviderHelp: Per-provider tool allow/deny overrides keyed by channel/provider ID to tailor capabilities by surface.
openclaw.configToolsByProviderJsonHelp: Per-provider policy object (optional allow, alsoAllow, deny, profile). Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configToolsElevatedHelp: Elevated tool access controls for privileged command surfaces that should only be reachable from trusted senders. Keep disabled unless operator workflows explicitly require elevated actions.
openclaw.configToolsElevatedEnabledHelp: Enables elevated tool execution path when sender and policy checks pass. Keep disabled in public/shared channels and enable only for trusted owner-operated contexts.
openclaw.configToolsElevatedAllowFromHelp: Sender allow rules for elevated tools, keyed by channel/provider identity formats. Use narrow, explicit identities.
openclaw.configToolsNestedPoliciesIntro: Edit structured sub-objects as JSON. Leave empty to omit. Invalid JSON is ignored on blur until fixed.
openclaw.configToolsJsonWebHelp: Web-tool policy grouping for search/fetch providers, limits, and fallback behavior tuning.
openclaw.configToolsJsonMediaHelp: Shared media understanding tool configuration (image, audio, video) and concurrency.
openclaw.configToolsJsonLoopHelp: Repetitive tool-call loop detection and backoff safety checks.
openclaw.configToolsJsonMessageHelp: Cross-context send, markers, and broadcast tool policy.
openclaw.configToolsJsonExecHelp: Exec-tool policy: host, security mode, approvals, timeouts, safe bins, and apply_patch.
openclaw.configToolsJsonFsHelp: Filesystem tool policy such as workspace-only restrictions.
openclaw.configToolsJsonSubagentsHelp: Tool policy wrapper for spawned subagents (tools.tools nested policy).
openclaw.configToolsJsonSandboxHelp: Tool policy applied when agents run in sandboxed execution environments.
openclaw.configMemoryIntro: Choose the global memory engine, citation visibility, and optional QMD sidecar settings when using the qmd backend.
openclaw.configMemoryBackendHelp: Selects the global memory engine: "builtin" uses OpenClaw memory internals, while "qmd" uses the QMD sidecar pipeline. Keep "builtin" unless you intentionally operate QMD.
openclaw.configMemoryCitationsHelp: Controls citation visibility in replies: "auto" shows citations when useful, "on" always shows them, and "off" hides them. Keep "auto" for a balanced signal-to-noise default.
openclaw.configMemoryQmdHelp: Optional QMD sidecar object (command, mcporter, searchMode, paths, sessions, update, limits, scope). Leave empty to omit memory.qmd. Invalid JSON on blur is ignored.
openclaw.configSessionIntro: Global session routing, reset, delivery policy, and maintenance controls for conversation history behavior. Keep defaults unless you need stricter isolation, retention, or delivery constraints.
openclaw.configSessionScopeHelp: Sets base session grouping strategy: "per-sender" isolates by sender and "global" shares one session per channel context. Keep "per-sender" for safer multi-user behavior unless deliberate shared context is required.
openclaw.configSessionDmScopeHelp: DM session scoping: "main" keeps continuity, while "per-peer", "per-channel-peer", and "per-account-channel-peer" increase isolation. Use isolated modes for shared inboxes or multi-account deployments.
openclaw.configSessionStoreHelp: Sets the session storage file path used to persist session records across restarts. Use an explicit path only when you need custom disk layout, backup routing, or mounted-volume storage.
openclaw.configSessionMainKeyHelp: Overrides the canonical main session key used for continuity when dmScope or routing logic points to "main". Use a stable value only if you intentionally need custom session anchoring.
openclaw.configSessionTypingModeHelp: Controls typing behavior timing: "never", "instant", "thinking", or "message" based emission points. Keep conservative modes in high-volume channels to avoid unnecessary typing noise.
openclaw.configSessionTypingIntervalHelp: Controls interval for repeated typing indicators while replies are being prepared in typing-capable channels. Increase to reduce chatty updates or decrease for more active typing feedback.
openclaw.configSessionIdleMinutesHelp: Applies a legacy idle reset window in minutes for session reuse behavior across inactivity gaps. Use this only for compatibility and prefer structured reset policies under session.reset / session.resetByType.
openclaw.configSessionParentForkMaxTokensHelp: Maximum parent-session token count allowed for thread/session inheritance forking. If the parent exceeds this, OpenClaw starts a fresh thread session instead of forking; set 0 to disable this protection.
openclaw.configSessionResetHelp: Defines the default reset policy object used when no type-specific or channel-specific override applies. Set this first, then layer resetByType or resetByChannel only where behavior must differ.
openclaw.configSessionResetModeHelp: Selects reset strategy: "daily" resets at a configured hour and "idle" resets after inactivity windows. Keep one clear mode per policy to avoid surprising context turnover patterns.
openclaw.configSessionResetAtHourHelp: Sets local-hour boundary (0-23) for daily reset mode so sessions roll over at predictable times. Use with mode=daily and align to operator timezone expectations for human-readable behavior.
openclaw.configSessionResetIdleMinutesHelp: Sets inactivity window before reset for idle mode and can also act as secondary guard with daily mode. Use larger values to preserve continuity or smaller values for fresher short-lived threads.
openclaw.configSessionAgentToAgentHelp: Groups controls for inter-agent session exchanges, including loop prevention limits on reply chaining. Keep defaults unless you run advanced agent-to-agent automation with strict turn caps.
openclaw.configSessionMaxPingPongHelp: Max reply-back turns between requester and target agents during agent-to-agent exchanges (0-5). Use lower values to hard-limit chatter loops and preserve predictable run completion.
openclaw.configSessionThreadBindingsHelp: Shared defaults for thread-bound session routing behavior across providers that support thread focus workflows. Configure global defaults here and override per channel only when behavior differs.
openclaw.configSessionThreadBindingsEnabledHelp: Global master switch for thread-bound session routing features and focused thread delivery behavior. Keep enabled for modern thread workflows unless you need to disable thread binding globally.
openclaw.configSessionThreadIdleHoursHelp: Default inactivity window in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables idle auto-unfocus). Default: 24.
openclaw.configSessionThreadMaxAgeHoursHelp: Optional hard max age in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables hard cap). Default: 0.
openclaw.configSessionResetTriggersHelp: Lists message triggers that force a session reset when matched in inbound content. Use sparingly for explicit reset phrases so context is not dropped unexpectedly during normal conversation. One trigger per line.
openclaw.configSessionAdvancedJsonIntro: Edit nested objects as JSON; leave empty to omit the key. Invalid JSON on blur is ignored.
openclaw.configSessionJsonResetByTypeHelp: Overrides reset behavior by chat type (direct, group, thread) when defaults are not sufficient.
openclaw.configSessionJsonResetByChannelHelp: Channel-specific reset overrides keyed by provider/channel id for fine-grained behavior control.
openclaw.configSessionJsonSendPolicyHelp: Controls cross-session send permissions using allow/deny rules evaluated against channel, chatType, and key prefixes.
openclaw.configSessionJsonIdentityLinksHelp: Maps canonical identities to provider-prefixed peer IDs so equivalent users resolve to one DM thread (JSON object of string to string[]).
openclaw.configSessionJsonMaintenanceHelp: Automatic session-store maintenance controls for pruning age, entry caps, and file rotation behavior. Start in warn mode to observe impact, then enforce once thresholds are tuned.
